This mechanism offers a clear pathway to identify specific signatures within MMO patterns and to map out the specific boundary that triggers a system's transition from a regime shift. a strong geodetic set is defined as a vertex set \( S \subseteq V(G) \) that allows covering all nodes within \(V(G) \setminus S\) by utilizing unique shortest paths between every distinct vertex pair within \( S \). The Strong Geodetic Decision problem involves taking a graph \( G \) and an integer \( k \) and determining whether \( G \) possesses a strong geodetic set no larger than \( k \). This issue has already been characterized as NP-hard on general graphs. This paper defines a new variant called the Strong Geodetic Recognition problem, which asks to verify if a specific provided subset \( S \subseteq V(G) \) qualifies as a strong geodetic set. We establish that this specific problem is also NP-hard. models of light propagation grounded in the parametrised post-Newtonian (PPN) formalism, a framework used to investigate potential general relativistic violations in observational data. Consequently, this work demonstrates that the Gaia parallax zero point is sensitive not only to errors in PPN $\gamma$ but also to uncertainties regarding the spacecraft's rotation.
